name: Skinwire
manufacturer: Unknown; suspected Nightshade Pharmatech gray-market derivative
description: A dermal suspension of nano-scale conductive filaments — stripped from decommissioned haptic suit liners — suspended in a biologically active carrier gel that promotes temporary subcutaneous integration. Applied as a patch, Skinwire creates a web of conductive tissue just below the skin surface, dramatically amplifying tactile sensation across the application area. Used recreationally for pleasure, practically by surgeons and safe-crackers who need extreme touch sensitivity, and dangerously by fighters who want to feel every impact with perfect clarity.
effects: extreme tactile sensitivity in application area
ability to feel microscopic surface textures
side_effects: filaments can migrate under the skin causing internal lacerations
hypersensitivity becoming painful allergy to normal touch
skin discoloration — faint silver tracery visible under bright light
in rare cases, filament migration to nerve clusters causing permanent altered sensation
duration: 12-24 hours per patch, with residual filaments persisting 2-3 days
cultural_context: Skinwire occupies an uncomfortable legal gray zone — the individual components are not illegal, and legitimate medical versions exist for surgical applications, but the street version uses unsterilized filaments and uncontrolled carrier gel. It's used in the Shelf's pleasure trade, by thieves and specialists, and by a subculture of Shelf fighters who compete in bare-knuckle bouts where the enhanced sensation is both advantage and spectacle.
story_hooks: A series of Shelf residents have been found with Skinwire filaments that have migrated to their spinal columns — someone modified the carrier gel to direct filament migration, and it's not clear whether it's an accident or an experiment
A Tier 3 safe-cracker has been using Skinwire to pull off impossible jobs — they've been leaving a deliberate silver trace on every vault they open, like a signature

The street Skinwire supply has been traced back to a Nightshade Pharmatech subsidiary that's been deliberately undercutting the medical market — the question is what they're getting out of having uncontrolled filaments distributed across the Shelf population
